SMTO-GWT-0081 — This GPU request was already sent once

GUID: 80c5b8cb-7fea-5c9d-b80c-4ecb1d29a50f
Slug: gpu-duplicate-operation
Domain: GWT · Subsystem: gpu

What happened

  • SMTO received a GPU request it had already seen, or one it couldn't record as new. The first copy may have run, so SMTO didn't run it again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the conversation, ask SMTO to show the current details for this GPU, without asking for any change. This shows whether the earlier request already set the value you wanted.
  2. If the change is already in place, stop there; nothing more is needed. SMTO refused the repeat so the same change wouldn't be applied twice.
  3. If the old value is still shown and no other task is working on this GPU, ask SMTO for the change again in a new message. Don't repeat clock or reset requests. A new message creates a fresh request, which SMTO handles separately from the earlier one.

What success looks like

  • The GPU details show the setting you wanted, and the change was made only once.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO; they identify the earlier request. Don't resend clock or reset changes to check whether the first one worked.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • GPU admission found this execution ID already active or remembered as finished (IDs are kept for 10 minutes), or the Gateway job registry refused to register job gpu_ plus the execution ID as new, in which case the effect is marked unknown.

What this means

  • GPU admission found the execution ID already active or finished, or durable foreground registration could not establish a fresh claim. The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.

Why this can happen

  • GPU admission found the execution ID already active or finished, or durable foreground registration could not establish a fresh claim.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the existing execution and durable job receipt for the same ID; do not generate a replacement ID to evade duplicate protection.

How to fix it

  • Look up the Gateway job named gpu_ plus the execution ID and the earlier receipt for that execution ID, and read gpu.device for the exact UUID. Do not replay the configuration request; issue a genuinely new change with a fresh execution ID only after the original is reconciled.
  • Inspect the existing result and current UUID state; do not replay the configuration request.

Retry and execution caution

  • For a mutation, inspect the exact UUID and resolve any active execution or uncertain effect before issuing a new operation. Never replay a reset or an unobservable clock change to infer its result.

How to verify the fix

  • The original operation's result and UUID state are reconciled before separately authorized new work.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, kill GPU clients automatically or invent sensor values.

Technical notes

  • The retained phase, target and receipt determine what executed. Rendering this definition adds no probe, retries, dispatch or changes to resource ownership.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
